newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Citroen says 1996 net just above zero.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Citroen says 1996 net just above zero.

text.p: Slovenian car trader Citroen Slovenia, fully owned by French group Citroen, said on Tuesday 1996 net profit was just above zero due to the company's substantial investments.

"It was very hard to make profits in the last four months of the year....most of it was invested into building up a fresh image of the company in Slovenia," Vincent Worbe, financial manager of Citroen Slovenia, told Reuters.
Citroen Slovenia started up operations last August when it took over sales of Citroen cars from Slovenia's troubled car parts producer Cimos.
The company said it did not expect to make a profit in the next couple of years due to stepped-up investments.

"In the last four months of 1996 we sold 542 cars, while this year we already managed to sell 730 cars and we expect to sell a total of 3,300 cars by the end of the year," Teran Ales, the firm's commercial manager said.
Sales in 1996 reached some 15 million marks ($8.8 million) and are expected to rise to 70 million marks ($40.9 million) this year.
Citroen plans to increase its market share in the tiny Alpine republic to around five percent this year from 1.2 percent in 1996.
"A fall in prices of our cars, which are up to 15 percent lower than last year, and more aggressive advertising are the main reasons for expected higher sales," Teran said.

The company expects to boost its sales further by opening five new showrooms by the end of the year, raising the total number of shops in Slovenia to 25. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
